title: subagent agent.json
description: The settings file of one agent folder under tools.native.subagent.agents_dir (Go backend only). Every key is optional: a folder may hold only prompt.md. The agent name is the folder name. The same keys are accepted inline under tools.native.subagent.agents.<name> in setting.json. Relative paths in model and prompt_documents resolve from the folder that holds this file.

description.description: Shown to the model in the tool description, so keep it short.

model.description: Model for this agent. In a catalog-layout session a value that does not end in .json is a model ID '<category>/<name>' of the models catalog; the agent may name any model of it, not only those its caller's profile lists. A value ending in .json is a model file, relative to the agent's folder or absolute. A legacy session reads every value as a file path (relative to the session directory for an inline agent). Absent means the calling session's model.

instructions.description: System prompt of the agent. The calling session's prompt is not used.

prompt_documents.description: Files appended to the agent's prompt after instructions (and after prompt.md for a folder agent), each separated by a blank line. A relative path is taken from the session's cwd, or from the agent's folder for a folder agent; ~ is expanded. The files are read when the session loads, and a missing file is a configuration error. The calling session's own prompt_documents are not used.

tools.description: Tools the agent may use: enabled read-only tools by name (read, grep, glob, fetch, skill, decide), and with allow_write also write, edit, bash, exec and process (listing one without allow_write is a configuration error; a child that lists process sees and stops only the processes it started, and they are stopped when its run ends), and MCP tools by ID, written mcp:<server>:<tool> (the server id from mcp_servers and the tool name the server reports). Absent means every enabled read-only native or extension tool and no MCP tool. An MCP tool is never added because its server calls it read-only: you name each one, so you vouch that it cannot change anything you care about. mcp:<server>:* gives the agent every loaded tool of that server (each once, even if also named exactly); a tool of a server whose approval is ask is skipped by the wildcard, and a wildcard left with no tool is a configuration error naming the server. A tool of a server whose approval is ask that is named exactly is refused, because a sub-agent has no way to ask the user. An agent that lists write, edit, bash or exec asks the user for those tools the same way the session does (their own approval setting applies), takes the checkpoint like a write, and runs to its end instead of being handed off unless tools.native.subagent.background_writers is on and none of its tools asks for approval. A name that is not loaded is a configuration error that lists the loaded ones; it is checked when the session loads.

toolset.description: One toolset file or a list of them, each '<category>/<name>' under the tools catalog (catalog-layout session only). The agent takes its tools, with their settings, and its MCP servers from it (or them) instead of the session's own toolset, so the profile does not have to register them and the parent never sees them. 'tools' still narrows within it and its mcp:<server>:<tool> entries are resolved against this file's servers only. The profile's tools.deny, allow_write and each tool's own paths and approval still apply. The toolset's subagent entry is ignored, so an agent that names a toolset cannot list subagent. A sub-agent's toolset must not set tools.native.profile_message. An unknown toolset is a configuration error that lists the available ones. Given a list, the toolsets merge in order: when two name the same native tool or MCP server the first listed wins, with a warning, and only the first toolset with hooks supplies hooks (a later one's hooks are ignored with a warning). Absent means the session's toolset.

max_tool_rounds.description: Most tool rounds of one run.

max_run_tokens.description: Most tokens one run may use before it starts another provider round. Absent means no cap.

auto_compaction.description: Whether this agent's child compacts its own transcript when it grows. Absent follows the session's compaction.auto_enabled, or is on when compaction_trigger_tokens is set.

compaction_trigger_tokens.description: Input size, in tokens, at which this agent's child compacts. Absent uses the session's compaction.trigger_tokens, which is sized for the master's model, so set it for a model with a different context window or price. Not allowed with auto_compaction false.

state_context.description: Send the newest state-context block stored for the session to this agent's child, in every request. A child collects none of its own. Nothing is sent when the session's statecontext is off or has no block yet.

timeout_ms.description: Wall-clock limit of one run, including provider waits.

allow.description: The agent's write and edit may change only paths inside one of these. A relative entry is taken from the workspace root. Narrows the session's own write and edit rules, never widens them.

deny.description: The agent's write and edit may not change a path inside any of these, even one allow permits.

paths.description: Narrows where this agent's write and edit may change files, on top of the session's rules. Only allowed for an agent that lists write or edit and no bash, exec or process: a shell can change any path, so a paths list cannot confine it and the combination is refused.
